draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kadalundi! This is where the Kadalundi River meets the Arabian Sea, and the cluster of islands at its mouth is a bird sanctuary. The estuary was also declared Kerala's very first community reserve.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat out here, so ask a local where they'd go for lunch.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Kadalundi–Vallikkunnu Community Reserve is about a 16 min walk, and Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary is around 23 min, on the islands where the river flows into the sea.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head for Kadalundi Nagaram beach, where the river joins the sea at the estuary the locals call the Azhimukham.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The railway through here is part of the oldest line in Kerala, laid in 1861 from Tirur to Chaliyam via Kadalundi.

spots.name: Vallikkunnu
spots.detail: 14 min walk · Village on the Kadalundi River

tips.title: Go early for the birds.
tips.body: The sanctuary spreads over islands at the river mouth, and the quiet morning hours are best for spotting birds.

tips.title: Find the estuary.
tips.body: The Kadalundi River meets the Arabian Sea at Kadalundi Nagaram beach, inside Vallikkunnu panchayat.

story.title: Kerala's first railway
story.body: One of Kerala's oldest railway lines was laid from Tirur to Chaliyam, passing through Vallikkunnu and Kadalundi.

story.title: Best panchayat
story.body: Vallikkunnu, right next door, was named the best panchayat in Kerala.

story.title: The bridge disaster
story.body: On 22 June 2001 a Mangalore-Chennai Mail fell into the Kadalundi river when a pillar of the 140-year-old bridge sank after heavy rain. 59 people were reported killed or missing.

story.title: A reserve for everyone
story.body: In April 2018 the forest department declared the Kadalundi–Vallikkunnu Community Reserve an ecotourism centre.
